mainTopicBrief: 本单元跨越两段伟大变革，涵盖郑和下西洋（Reading）、海上历险记（Extended reading）和工业革命与城市化（Integrated skills）三个子话题——历史人物介绍与家乡变迁是高考应用文的常见场景，历史价值与城市化更是雅思社会类议论文的传统命题。

subTopics.title: 郑和下西洋
subTopics.desc: 课文核心：navigators took compass readings, kept logs of their voyages and charted the coast——郑和的远航 helped develop and strengthen harmonious relations，exposing foreign people to Chinese culture。

prompts.task: 你的英国笔友 Alex 对中国历史上的著名探险家很感兴趣。请你用英文回信介绍郑和，内容包括：1. 郑和远航的概况；2. 远航的意义；3. 你的评价。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Alex,

You asked me about great explorers in Chinese history, and the first name that comes to my mind is Zheng He.

About six hundred years ago, he set sail from China and led seven great voyages across the ocean. As they sailed, the navigators took compass readings, kept logs of their voyages and charted the coast. More importantly, Zheng He's efforts helped develop and strengthen harmonious relations with the countries he visited, exposing foreign people to Chinese culture and allowing the Chinese to better understand overseas lands.

What I admire most is that his mighty fleet came in peace, not for conquest. If you are interested, I can send you a documentary about him.

Yours,
Li Hua
vocabHints: expose foreign people to Chinese culture

prompts.task: Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects, while others think that, in today's world, subjects like science and technology matter more. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
School timetables are a quiet battlefield: some insist history deserves a central place, while others would hand its hours to science and technology, the engines of modern economies. Having weighed both views, I believe the two are complementary, though I would resist any further shrinking of history.

The champions of science hold strong cards. Technical skills lead directly to employment, national prosperity now rests on innovation, and citizens who misunderstand data or medicine make costly choices. In a world of algorithms and vaccines, scientific literacy is a form of self-defence, and countries that neglect it fall behind visibly and fast.

Yet the case for history is equally practical, if less obvious. History is the laboratory of human behaviour: it shows how wars begin, how economies collapse, how propaganda works and how rights were won, and citizens ignorant of these patterns are easily manipulated by those who are not. Voters, after all, are asked to judge questions — of war, trade and liberty — that are historical in nature. History also trains the weighing of evidence and of conflicting accounts, a skill identical in spirit to scientific method, and it anchors identity: a community that forgets its past loses the thread of who it is.

The choice, moreover, is false. A curriculum can teach both, and the most valuable graduates combine them — engineers who understand the social consequences of technology, and policymakers who understand what technology can and cannot do.

In conclusion, science equips societies to build the future, while history equips them to choose it wisely. Schools should refuse the either-or and teach the two as partners.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):双方论据均衡有力(科学方:就业/国家竞争/公民科学素养;历史方:行为实验室/选民判断/证据训练/身份认同)，立场'互补+反对继续压缩历史'具体可辨，并指出题目二选一预设为假。
Coherence & Cohesion(连贯衔接):champions of science / Yet the case for history / moreover / In conclusion 交锋式推进;'History is the laboratory of human behaviour'的核心隐喻统领历史段四个how排比。
Lexical Resource(词汇资源):hold strong cards / a form of self-defence / loses the thread of who it is / refuse the either-or 等表达凝练;engines of modern economies同位语开题定调。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法多样性):if less obvious省略让步、破折号插入限定(of war, trade and liberty)、who定语从句双层嵌套、平行收尾(build the future / choose it wisely)。
vsGaokao: 体裁:高考写介绍郑和的回信(史实+意义+评价);雅思写学科价值双边议论文。
论据来源:高考信件严格织入课文'took compass readings / harmonious relations'词块;雅思用课程论与公民教育的普适论据，不提郑和。
语域:书信亲切分享(the first name that comes to my mind);雅思论证冷静，比喻服务论点。
评分维度:高考重史实准确+情感真挚;雅思discuss题的高分在于超越站队——'互补+底线'立场展示层次。

subTopics.title: 海上历险记
subTopics.desc: 拓展阅读核心：风暴之夜，Russell felt his blood freeze, but he quickly came to himself and rushed up to the deck——恐惧之中的行动力，才是冒险故事真正的主角。

prompts.task: 你校读书节正在征集英文荐书稿。请你推荐一本你读过的航海冒险小说，内容包括：1. 书的基本内容；2. 印象最深的情节；3. 推荐理由。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Hello, everyone! At this year's Reading Festival, I would like to recommend a sea adventure novel that kept me up half the night.

The story follows a young sailor named Russell on his first ocean voyage. When a terrible storm strikes at midnight, "Russell felt his blood freeze, but he quickly came to himself and rushed up to the deck." From that page on, I was standing beside him — soaked, terrified and determined.

What makes the book special is not the storm itself, but how an ordinary boy learns courage: not the absence of fear, but the strength to act in spite of it.

If you long for the sea and a test of the heart, this voyage is for you.
vocabHints: keep me up half the night

prompts.task: Many people take part in dangerous activities such as sailing across oceans, climbing high mountains or extreme sports. Why do people take these risks? What can be done to reduce the dangers involved? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
From mountaineering to ocean sailing, millions deliberately seek activities in which mistakes can be fatal. This essay considers why danger attracts people and how its risks can be reduced.

The motives run deeper than recklessness. Modern life is safe and scheduled, and many feel that comfort has crowded out intensity; extreme activities restore the concentration and self-reliance that routine rarely demands. Physiology plays its part — fear releases adrenalin, and mastering it produces a euphoria that ordinary exercise cannot match. For others the appeal is identity and achievement: navigating a storm or reaching a summit provides proof of courage that no examination can certify. Social media has added a further push, turning daring feats into currency for admiration.

Risk, however, can be managed without abolishing the thrill. Proper training is the first safeguard: most accidents involve novices attempting conditions beyond their skill, so graduated qualifications — as diving and aviation already require — should become standard across adventure sports. Equipment and information come next: helmets, locator beacons, weather forecasts and route plans convert many potential tragedies into stories told afterwards. Organised structure helps too; clubs, licensed guides and rescue insurance ensure that when things go wrong, help arrives quickly and the cost does not fall on the public. Finally, honest media portrayals that show the years of preparation, not just the moment of triumph, would correct the illusion that daring alone is enough.

In conclusion, people pursue danger to feel fully alive and to prove themselves against something real. Since the impulse is ancient and will not disappear, the sensible response is not prohibition but training, regulation and rescue — keeping the adventure while shrinking the gamble.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):两问齐答且分量均衡——动机段四层(补偿安全生活/生理机制/身份证明/社媒推动)，对策段四招(分级资质/装备信息/组织保障/媒体真实呈现)，结论明确反对禁止路线。
Coherence & Cohesion(连贯衔接):首段直接预告双问结构;动机与对策段内均用first/next/too/Finally显性排序;'keeping the adventure while shrinking the gamble'对仗收束两问。
Lexical Resource(词汇资源):comfort has crowded out intensity / currency for admiration / graduated qualifications / tragedies into stories told afterwards 等表达精准生动。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法多样性):in which定语从句开题、破折号类比插入(as diving and aviation already require)、that no examination can certify否定限定、since原因从句推进结论。
vsGaokao: 体裁:高考写读书节荐书稿(内容+情节+理由);雅思写why+how双问分析文。
论据来源:高考荐书稿直接引用课文Russell风暴句作书中金句;雅思用冒险心理学与安全管理的普适论据。
语域:荐书稿有沉浸感染力(I was standing beside him);雅思冷静归因，抒情仅在fully alive一处。

subTopics.title: 广泛阅读的力量
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：extensive reading、facilitate learning、sort ... into、works of literature——从航海日志到工业史，广泛阅读为理解世界打开一扇又一扇门。

prompts.task: 你校图书馆将开展'广泛阅读月'活动。请你用英文写一篇短文投稿校刊，向同学们介绍广泛阅读的好处与方法，内容包括：1. 广泛阅读的益处；2. 你的两三条方法建议。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
This month our library is holding a "Wide Reading" campaign, and I'd like to share why it is worth joining.

Extensive reading does more than fill spare time; it quietly facilitates learning across every subject. History, science, travel logs, works of literature — each opens a door to a world we could not otherwise enter, and the more widely we read, the more easily new ideas connect.

Here are a few tips. First, read a little every day rather than a lot once in a while. Second, keep a simple notebook and sort useful words and quotations into topics. Third, don't be afraid to abandon a book you dislike — there are plenty more.

A wide reader is never bored, and never alone. Happy reading!
vocabHints: opens a door to a world
sort useful words and quotations into topics

prompts.task: Some people believe that reading widely across many subjects gives students the best education, while others think it is better to study a few subjects in depth. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Educators have long disagreed over how knowledge is best acquired: by reading broadly across many fields, or by studying a few subjects deeply. Both approaches have real strengths, and in my opinion the ideal education combines them, with breadth laying the foundation and depth built upon it.

Those who favour breadth argue that wide reading produces flexible, well-rounded minds. Exposure to history, science, literature and art helps students see connections between fields, adapt to a fast-changing world, and discover where their true interests lie. Many great insights, indeed, come from applying an idea in one discipline to a problem in another — a habit only broad learning makes possible. Wide reading also facilitates learning generally, since a rich store of background knowledge makes each new subject easier to grasp.

Supporters of depth reply that real mastery requires focus. Skimming many subjects can leave a student who knows a little about everything and nothing thoroughly, whereas concentrating on a few allows genuine expertise, the kind that advances knowledge and leads to serious careers. Modern professions, from medicine to engineering, demand precisely this depth.

The two aims, however, are complementary rather than opposed. A broad foundation in the early years helps students choose wisely and think across boundaries, while specialisation later turns that breadth into real competence. An education that offers only one leaves the mind either shallow or narrow.

In conclusion, while depth produces expertise and breadth produces perspective, the best education needs both. Students should read widely to understand the world, then dig deeply into the fields that will define their working lives.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):双观点均充分(广度:灵活视野/跨学科洞见;深度:真正精通/职业需求)，立场'广度打基础、深度筑其上'的结合式主张清晰，结论明确。
Coherence & Cohesion(连贯衔接):favour breadth / Supporters of depth reply / however complementary / In conclusion 推进工整;'facilitates learning'织入单元词块;结尾'read widely then dig deeply'收束。
Lexical Resource(词汇资源):well-rounded minds / a rich store of background knowledge / genuine expertise / think across boundaries 表达精准。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法多样性):破折号插入跨学科例证、whereas对比、rather than opposed、while对比收尾，句式多样。
vsGaokao: 体裁:高考写广泛阅读投稿(益处+方法);雅思写广度vs深度学习双边议论文。
论据来源:高考短文织入课件'extensive reading / facilitate learning / sort...into / works of literature'词块;雅思用教育论的普适论据。
语域:短文亲切建议(Happy reading!);雅思学术权衡，结合式立场显层次。
评分维度:高考重方法可行+益处;雅思discuss题高分在于整合而非站队——'广度筑基、深度其上'是思辨核心。

subTopics.title: 工业革命与城市化
subTopics.desc: 综合板块核心：the shift from the cottage industry to the factory system... promoted economic growth and expanded world trade——thousands migrated from rural to urban areas in search of work。

prompts.task: 你校英文报开设 "My Hometown's Story" 专栏。请你采访长辈后写一篇短文，讲述家乡从乡村到城市的变迁，内容包括：1. 过去的样子；2. 变化及原因；3. 你的感受。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
My grandfather often says that his childhood village and my city are two different worlds, though they share the same name.

Decades ago, most work there was done at home or in the fields. Then factories arrived, and thousands migrated from rural to urban areas in search of work — my grandparents among them. Machines changed everything: goods that had once been made slowly by hand could now be produced in factories, where each worker had a specialized role. Economic growth brought wider roads, taller buildings and better schools.

Something was lost, too — the slow evenings my grandfather still misses. But when I asked whether he would go back, he smiled and shook his head. Progress, he said, is a one-way journey.
vocabHints: the work was done at home
migrate from rural to urban areas
each worker had a specialized role

prompts.task: In many countries, more and more people move from the countryside to big cities. Do you think this is a positive or negative development? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
In most developing countries, millions leave villages each year in search of work and opportunity in cities. I regard this migration as a broadly positive development, provided governments manage its pressures deliberately.

The gains begin with the migrants themselves. Cities concentrate jobs, schools, hospitals and ideas, so a family's move often multiplies its income and transforms its children's prospects within a generation. Economies benefit in parallel: industry and services find the workers they need, productivity rises, and the money migrants send home rebuilds the villages they left. History suggests the pattern is no accident — every industrialised nation travelled the same road from field to factory to office, and urbanisation has accompanied nearly every escape from mass poverty in the modern era.

The costs, nonetheless, are real. Cities that grow faster than their infrastructure produce slums, congestion and overstretched services; migrants can face insecurity and discrimination far from family networks; and the countryside may be left with an ageing population and abandoned land. Where governance is weak, these strains harden into permanent inequality between gleaming centres and neglected peripheries.

Yet such problems indict poor management rather than migration itself. Investment in affordable housing, transport and schools lets cities absorb newcomers productively; equal access to public services prevents a two-class citizenry; and rural development — roads, clinics, modern agriculture — gives those who stay behind a genuine choice rather than a sentence.

In conclusion, the movement from countryside to city is the engine by which poor economies become richer ones. Handled with foresight, its benefits to individuals and nations clearly outweigh its costs.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):positive/negative题给出'总体积极+管理前提'的清晰裁决;收益从个体、经济、历史规律三层展开，代价段诚实充分后用'indict poor management rather than migration itself'完成归因反转。
Coherence & Cohesion(连贯衔接):gains / costs, nonetheless / Yet / In conclusion 骨架工整;'from field to factory to office'的三步走意象浓缩历史论据;三个分号并列的治理方案与三项代价一一呼应。
Lexical Resource(词汇资源):multiplies its income / overstretched services / gleaming centres and neglected peripheries / a two-class citizenry / a genuine choice rather than a sentence 表达密度高且精准。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法多样性):provided条件句、so结果从句、Where状语从句、by which定语从句收束比喻(the engine by which...)，句式层次丰富。

论据来源:高考短文织入课文'migrated from rural to urban areas / specialized role'词块并借祖辈口述;雅思用发展经济学普适论据(汇款、基建、治理)。
